newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close up on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close up on fresh buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed up on Wednesday on fresh buying by a few big textile mills which were piling up their stocks, dealers said.

They said rates were likely to open mixed on Thursday, but it was not clear if the market at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) would be open. Opposition parties have called a strike to protest at last Friday's killing of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
Kerb rates for NIAB-78 fluctuated between 2,100 and 2,150 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), broker Nasim Usman said, as rumours of a bumper harves alternated with rumours of crop damage.
